text.title: Distribution Channel Research Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether a converting offer exists at all, whether one channel already shows channel-market fit, and whether gross profit per customer is known well enough to compute payback in months — to a full channel scoring run, a halt on unit economics, or a skip.

decision-tree.root-question: Has the product taken money from anyone through any route, so a conversion rate exists to score channels against?

branch.when: zero paying customers from any source, or the whole test budget cannot fund even one channel above its noise floor

conclusion.verdict: skip; emit a structured skip — there is nothing to place yet. Establish a converting offer through direct outreach before scoring paid or organic channels

branch.when: customers are converting through at least one identifiable route
branch.question: Is one channel already delivering repeatable acquisition at acceptable cost, or is spend scattered with no clear winner?

branch.when: one channel already shows channel-market fit and is not yet saturated

conclusion.verdict: skip; concentrate on the working channel until it saturates — scoring alternatives now splits attention and budget away from a proven route

branch.when: no channel is clearly working, or the current one is saturating and a second is needed
branch.question: Is monthly gross profit per customer known — margin, retention and ACV — so CAC payback in months can actually be computed per row?

branch.when: only revenue is known; margin or retention are guesses, so payback cannot be computed

conclusion.verdict: halt; establish gross margin and monthly gross profit per customer first — raw CAC without payback months cannot gate a channel score

branch.when: gross profit per customer per month and retention are known well enough to compute payback and LTV:CAC

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; declare one CAC definition and one horizon across all rows, keep TTFR separate, and ship at most 3 channels with one primary and a committed kill number each
